description: Explicit exceptions and product decisions for repository-discovered frontend surface families. Discovery remains fail-closed; absence of a matching rule blocks dispatch.

rules.rationale: The dependency-light public platform shell and browser-safe catalog are the governed entrypoint for the unified frontend.
The host-scoped root handler returns public discovery metadata for every registered method and is consumed as API bootstrap data, not as a standalone product surface.
Existing Connect assets remain a compatibility surface while the unified shell is introduced.
Existing Local Manager browser pages remain supported until wave F4 reaches verified parity.
Health contracts feed status components but are not standalone navigation destinations.
Status contracts feed operational views but are not standalone navigation destinations.
The overlay exposes JWT-scoped Activation session context and safe session metadata as OAuth API responses consumed by the Tenant Activation GPT; it does not render a standalone browser surface.
Session reference, turn, and closure handlers are authenticated archive APIs consumed by governed GPT and Activation clients; they are not independent navigation or embedded UI surfaces.

Hash-only runtime binding and Hostinger bootstrap dry-run evidence are protected internal operational APIs, not browser navigation surfaces. They remain read-only and service-key-only, and the dry-run cannot authorize migrations, grants, deployment, or restart.

Environment-scoped Runtime Breakglass status, planning, dispatch, and bounded readback are internal service-key operational contracts. They are not browser navigation surfaces, do not expose credentials or database names, and remain subject to exact-SHA, plan, confirmation, and readback controls.
Database-independent Admin recovery API is exposed only through the bounded Admin Core action surface; it is not a browser navigation surface and does not itself grant mutation authority.

The Staging Recovery Admin surface is a private API-only contract for activation-dev readiness and certification status. It is not a browser navigation surface, advertises GET-only operations, forbids Production authority, and keeps consequential certification in a separate workflow.

The Recovery Kernel is a private, Production-only administrative API and fixed system dispatcher. It is not a browser navigation surface, never accepts raw commands or credentials, and keeps consequential execution behind plan, approval, lock, idempotency, and readback gates.
